source_text: νατος οὐ πρὸς ἀδοξίαν ἔσται ποθὲν, ἀλλ' εἰς λαμπρὰν καὶ ἐμφανεστάτην ἐκτελευτήσει δόξαν. Ἐν εἴδει γὰρ δὴ τῷ πυρὸς νοεῖται τὸ θεῖον· καταβέβηκε δὲ οὕτως καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος τὸ Σινᾶ. Καταλύσων δὲ τοῦ θανάτου τὸ κράτος, ὑπέδυ τὸν θάνατον οἰκονομικ
pass_a_gloss: …pyr theion… Sinā… thanatos eis doxan… ēskēnōsen en hēmin…
pass_b_english: Cyril: …death will not be somehow unto dishonor, but will finish out unto bright and most manifest glory. For in a form at least of fire the divine is thought; and thus it has also come down upon the mountain Sinai. And about to loose the power of death, Christ has entered under death economically, that as God he may be glorified by us. So then the death creeps unto God-fitting glory, having as end the bright living-again, and the small-fitting in the suffering, being conquered by the uppermost good-fames, goes away unto nothing; and this, I think, is riddlingly the being spent with fire of the dead calf. And having added, that for it is sin, he has made clear that the passion of Christ has come to be unto cleansing-off of sin, and the matter is not unclear.

Cyril: Then the first ram is taken and is slaughtered equally with the calf; and the blood again was being held toward the altar, and being cut limb-wise was being brought up, with the inwards having been washed with water, with head together and feet…
Palladius: And would someone think perhaps that even the life of Christ itself has come to be for us?

Cyril: And indeed you will know somehow also very easily, having thought that we have become sharers of the transgression in Adam, and all but have also paid the justices of the things failed by that one, with the curse having run through unto all, and the anger having somehow been distributed over the race from him. So then the Only-begotten has come down unto becoming-human, and has tented among us, and

choices.why: Divine glory; Sinai; passion unto glory.
